assessment.whats_new: Integration of an agentic LLM (Astra) directly with the After Effects API, allowing users to describe complex motion tasks (physics, rigging, re-layouts) which are then executed as native, editable AE layers and keyframes.
whats_transferable: Agentic DCC control: Using specialized LLM 'skills' to translate natural language into specific software API calls.
Automated ASCII conversion: Mapping brightness values of a source video to a grid of characters generated via an AI-authored script.
AI-driven physics simulation: Automating fall/rotate/bounce/settle keyframes for 2D layers without manual curve editing.
Dynamic re-layout: Using an agent to maintain spatial relationships and parent-child constraints when changing aspect ratios across multiple compositions.
assessment.pipeline_notes: While AE-focused, the logic of using an agent with specific 'skills' (scripts/plugins) to handle boilerplate rigging and layout tasks is highly applicable to Houdini or Maya pipelines. Shows how AI can convert storyboards from Figma into native, keyframed AE projects.
Features a custom Python-based ASCII video converter that translates source video brightness into character-based transparent PNG sequences.
Automates complex 2D rigging and physics simulations (gravity and collisions) through natural language prompts.
Demonstrates massive time savings in 'versioning' tasks like project localization and aspect ratio adaptation (15 minutes vs 3 hours manual estimate).

assessment.whats_new: Jev is a specialized AI model from TypeSafe AI designed for fast decision-making instead of text generation. It uses Reinforcement Learning for Calibrated Decisions (RLCD) and parallel sampling to evaluate all potential answers simultaneously, making it up to 200x faster and significantly cheaper than traditional LLMs.
whats_transferable: Architectural separation of 'generative' tasks from 'decision' tasks to improve pipeline automation speed.
Implementation of calibrated confidence values to trigger human intervention or higher-fidelity fallbacks in automated scripts.
Offloading simple binary or multiple-choice logic from slow LLMs to fast, specialized classification models.
assessment.pipeline_notes: For a USD/Houdini TD, this model type could handle high-volume discrete logic tasks such as asset tagging, metadata validation, or automated QC checks during scene assembly without the latency of a standard LLM. It serves as a fast logic layer for autonomous agents in a production environment.
assessment.visual_quality_notes: The video demos focus on real-time response in low-fidelity games like Doom and Tetris; the relevance is purely on the speed of the decision logic rather than visual fidelity or rendering quality.
assessment.reason_if_low: While the decision-speed is impressive, the focus is on game agents and coding assistants rather than direct 3D/VFX production workflows.
summary_bullets: Jev is a decision-only model that avoids token generation to maximize speed and minimize token cost.
It employs RLCD to ensure that confidence scores represent actual probability of being correct, enabling reliable automated branching logic.
The model is built for System One (fast, intuitive) tasks, allowing heavier generative models to focus on complex reasoning.

assessment.whats_new: A production-tested hybrid animation pipeline that uses 3D layout as a motion reference for AI video generation, combined with highly structured 'system prompts' that explicitly include the 12 principles of animation.
whats_transferable: Structuring prompts into blocks: Scene Context, Active References, Shot Structure, and Constraints
Using grayscale 3D blocking videos as the primary motion signal for AI to control camera and character timing
Iterative keyframe correction where AI outputs are manually fixed in Photoshop and fed back as image references
assessment.pipeline_notes: This workflow bridges the gap between traditional layout/animation and AI rendering. In a USD pipeline, this would effectively replace the lighting/rendering/compositing stage with an AI 'stylization' pass conditioned on Anim/Layout exports.
assessment.visual_quality_notes: Achieves high temporal consistency for stylized characters by locking character sheets and 3D guides, though subtle character acting remains a bottleneck for the AI models.
summary_bullets: Adopts an 'asset-first' approach where character, prop, and location sheets are finalized and 'locked' before any video generation begins.
Utilizes a dual-path workflow: simple shots use direct text-to-video, while complex actions utilize Blender-based previs as video-to-video input.
Introduces the 'System Prompt' concept to Claude, creating a reusable structure that dictates style rules and physics for the AI model across the entire sequence.
Manages texture density conflicts by simplifying moving assets (clean 3D style) while maintaining complex textures (watercolor) for static backgrounds.
Demonstrates how 'subtle acting' gaps are currently the hardest part of the AI transition, requiring manual overrides or simplified shot designs.
